Figure 1: Core results. Across two policy models and three agentic benchmarks (ALFWorld, SearchQA, WebShop), TRIAGE consistently improves over the GRPO baseline (dashed line). Bar labels report mean success rate; vertical axes are truncated per panel to make differences visible.

Table 3: Main results: success rate (%). ALFWorld and WebShop entries with ± are mean ± sample standard deviation over ten independent training-and-evaluation runs. Search-QA is reported as a single run because the retrieval-augmented rollout loop makes repeated full training runs substantially more expensive. The “no evidence” rows use the same Qwen3-8B-thinking judge but with a prompt that does not ask for a per-segment evidence string and only requests the role label (see Appendix H for the full default prompt that does require evidence).

Figure 2: Overview of TRIAGE. Rollouts are split into environment-facing segments, a structured judge assigns semantic roles, and role-conditioned process rewards adjust segment-level GRPO advantages.
